when: Tests whether two categorical variables are related, or whether group membership and a categorical outcome are independent.
example: Imagine asking 100 students whether they prefer tea or coffee and noting each student's year of study. A chi-square test asks whether drink preference depends on year of study, or whether the two are unrelated.
small_sample: When the table is small or sparse the chi-square approximation breaks down. Switch to Fisher's exact test or simulate the p-value, and report Cramer's V with a confidence interval rather than the p-value alone.
assumptions: Observations are independent of one another
Each case appears in exactly one cell of the table
At least 80 per cent of expected cell counts are 5 or more, and none is below 1
alternative: Fisher's exact test, when expected counts are small in a 2 by 2 table

# survey_skeleton.R
# StatChooser sample survey skeleton (surveyframe method = "chi_square").
# Section A is a standard demographic block. Section B, and C/D/E where present,
# carry the measures the analysis plan needs. Replace every [bracketed] stem
# with your own validated items before fielding the survey.
# install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)

# ---- Choice sets (define once, reuse) ----
cat_set <- sf_choices("cat_set", 1:3, c("Category 1", "Category 2", "Category 3"))
gender_cs <- sf_choices("gender_cs",
  c("woman", "man", "nonbinary", "selfdescribe", "na"),
  c("Woman", "Man", "Non-binary", "Prefer to self-describe", "Prefer not to say"))
edu_cs <- sf_choices("edu_cs", 1:5,
  c("Secondary or below", "Diploma", "Bachelor degree", "Master degree", "Doctorate"))
role_cs <- sf_choices("role_cs", 1:4,
  c("Entry or junior", "Mid-level", "Senior or manager", "Executive or owner"))
industry_cs <- sf_choices("industry_cs", 1:5,
  c("Manufacturing", "Retail or trade", "Services", "Public sector", "Other"))

# ---- Section A: Respondent profile ----
sec_a <- sf_item("sec_a", "Section A: Respondent profile", type = "section_break",
  section_intro = "A few background questions about you.")
age <- sf_item("age", "Your age in years", type = "numeric")
gender <- sf_item("gender", "Your gender", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "gender_cs")
education <- sf_item("education", "Highest level of education completed", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "edu_cs")
job_role <- sf_item("job_role", "Your role or seniority", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "role_cs")
experience <- sf_item("experience", "Years of experience", type = "numeric")
industry <- sf_item("industry", "Your industry or sector", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "industry_cs")

# ---- Section B: Categorical variables ----
sec_b <- sf_item("sec_b", "Section B: Categorical variables", type = "section_break")
var_a <- sf_item("var_a", "[first categorical variable - replace]", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "cat_set")
var_b <- sf_item("var_b", "[second categorical variable - replace]", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "cat_set")

# ---- Analysis plan (ids match the items and scales above) ----
plan_entry <- list(
  id                = "RQ1",
  research_question = "Are the two categorical variables related?",
  family            = "association",
  method            = "chi_square",
  roles             = list(
    row        = "var_a",
    column     = "var_b"
  ),
  options           = list(alpha = 0.05)
)

# ---- Assemble the instrument ----
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title         = "[Your study title]",
  description   = "[Population and purpose]",
  components    = list(
    sec_a, age, gender, education, job_role, experience, industry, sec_b, var_a, var_b
  ),
  analysis_plan = list(plan_entry)
)
